answer: Each identity claims one canyon river reach, locks a 70 bond, and files an upstream stage log. A downstream mirror gauge bound to the same reach and key must file a matching log; the auditor recomputes expected flow from the public river table and burns the bond when logs differ by over 3% or a mirror signature is reused. The first filing costs 35, the kth costs 35+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7028 and 1000 fakes cost 3,531,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-mirror ring fails: one mirror gauge serves only one reach per epoch. An honest operator pays 35 once and redeems it after a clean audit.
